#### Ed Harmon

Ed Harmon, founder of NAI Harmon Group and Spartan Logistics, is a renowned entrepreneur driving economic and community development across the U.S. As Board of Directors Chairman, he brings expertise in leadership, sales, trucking, and real estate. Recognized in Columbus and Toledo for his innovation, he fosters business growth, job creation, and prosperity, serving on numerous boards, both profit and non-profit. His business model offers end-to-end real estate services, including development, brokerage, construction, property management, financing, and logistics. NAI Harmon Group, Ohio’s only full-service commercial real estate firm, and the Harmon Family businesses collectively own and manage 15 million square feet across 16 states.

 

#### Steve Harmon

###### Chief Executive Officer

Steve Harmon is an entrepreneur, CPA, industrial real estate investor, and logistics executive with more than 35 years of experience building and operating businesses at the intersection of supply chain and commercial real estate.

Steve serves as CEO of Spartan Logistics, a third party logistics company based in Columbus, Ohio and of NAI Harmon Group, a commercial real estate brokerage, property management, and development firm based in Toledo, Ohio.

During his tenure as President of Spartan Logistics from 2010 to 2021, Steve helped expand the company into a multi-state logistics provider with more than 20 locations. His experience operating warehouses led to a broader strategy of integrating logistics with industrial real estate ownership, development, construction, leasing, and property management.

Today, Steve focuses on business strategy, capital allocation, industrial real estate investment, leadership development, and the long-term growth of the Harmon family of companies.

A graduate of American University, Steve is a Certified Public Accountant and licensed Ohio real estate professional. Steve is also a Certified Executive Logistics Professional. He brings a finance-driven, operators perspective to real estate and believes the fundamentals of business remain simple: keep your promises, solve customers problems, develop great people, and execute consistently.

 

#### Josh Ledford

Josh Ledford’s logistics career started in 2001 as a temporary warehouse employee for Spartan Logistics, where he now serves as company President, overseeing the operational strategic plan and guidelines for Spartan business units throughout all of their locations and two corporate offices. 

In addition to managing distribution operations to ensure productivity and success at all levels, Josh strives to mentor his warehouse leaders and to support efficient company growth while providing outstanding customer service. By building and maintaining strong relationships with a wide variety of partners, he continues to assure Spartan’s place as an industry leader.

 

#### Craig Recker

###### Vice President of Operations

With over 21 years at Spartan Logistics, Craig Recker has been pivotal in shaping the company's operational success. As Vice President of Operations, he oversees warehouse management, logistics, inventory control, and supply chain strategies, ensuring efficient solutions for customers. A University of Toledo graduate with a degree in Marketing and Professional Sales, Craig combines leadership skills with expertise in operations management, customer service, and process improvement. His dedication to teamwork, excellence, and innovation has driven growth and customer satisfaction, making him a cornerstone of Spartan’s success.

 

#### Cindy Stafford

###### Director of Human Resources

With nearly 20 years of experience in Human Resources, Cindy serves as Spartan Logistics’ Director of Human Resources and is a member of the company’s Leadership Team. In addition to leading the HR function, she provides leadership and oversight for Spartan’s safety initiatives. Cindy works closely with leaders across the organization to strengthen Spartan’s culture, develop its people, and ensure HR strategies support the needs and continued growth of the business. A SHRM-CP and Qualified Warehouse Logistics Professional (QWLP), she brings a practical approach to HR leadership and is passionate about helping leaders and employees succeed.

Cindy holds a Master’s in Human Resources and Employment Law from Arizona State University and a Bachelor’s in Human Resources Management. She has presented at the IWLA Convention and HR Summit on a variety of workplace and leadership topics and has participated in industry panels, sharing her experience and perspective with other HR professionals.

 

#### Nick Harmon

###### Director of Business Development 

With six years of sales experience, Nick leads efforts to grow warehouse business across the Midwest and South, focusing on new prospects, expanding client relationships, and driving demand. His detail-oriented, communicative approach and industry expertise make him a key asset in fostering growth.

Nick holds a Bachelor’s Degree in Finance and Marketing from Mount Vernon Nazarene University. He has spoken at the International Warehouse Logistics Association’s 2022 Economics of Warehousing and 2023 Marketing Conference and is a member of the International Warehouse Logistics Association and the University of Toledo Family Business Center.

#### Rachael Walling

 With over six years in the logistics industry, Rachael Walling has developed expertise in contract management, customer engagement, billing audits, and relationship-building. As Director of Customer Experience at Spartan Logistics, she leads her team to enhance service quality and client satisfaction. Rachael is passionate about fostering strong client partnerships and tackling challenges. Her collaborative approach and leadership make her an invaluable asset in driving success and customer loyalty. She holds a Master’s in Clinical Mental Health Counseling and a Bachelor’s in Psychology from South University. She actively participates in industry associations like IWLA and is a Qualified Warehouse and Logistics Professional (QWLP), demonstrating her commitment to ongoing professional development in the logistics field. 

 

#### Sam Coil

With over 10 years of accounting experience, Sam applies her expertise to oversee the company’s finance functions, including Accounts Payable and Receivable, budget management, and strategic financial planning. She provides financial clarity to the team and works closely with operations managers to ensure profitability and efficiency. Sam holds a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration with an Accounting Specialization from The Ohio State University Fisher College of Business and is working towards her Qualified Warehouse Logistics Professional (QWLP) Certification through the IWLA.

 

#### Chuck Harrison

 With over 25 years of experience, Chuck specializes in data analytics, strategic planning, resource management, quality control, and compliance. He leads nine Ohio facilities, driving continuous improvement through agile methodologies and aligning operations with business goals. Chuck is passionate about mentoring teams, fostering collaboration, and enhancing supply chain efficiency by reducing costs, improving lead times, and maintaining quality. He has expertise in supply chain management, leadership, financial acumen, and technology integration. Chuck holds an Associate’s Degree in Operations Management/Supply Chain from Owens Community College. 

 

#### Matt Edwards

With over 20 years of experience, Matt specializes in 3PL, distribution, warehousing, and trucking logistics. He currently leads operations in IN, IL, MO, SC, AR, and TX, focusing on delivering safe, respectful, and team-driven service to customers. Matt is passionate about process-driven logistics and building strong, service-focused teams and leaders. His collaborative approach, balancing process optimization with leadership development, fosters both organizational and personal growth. Matt holds a B.S.B.A. in Transportation Logistics and a B.S.B.A. in Human Resource Management from the Sam M. Walton College of Business.

#### Troy Leming

Troy Leming serves as Director of Operations at Spartan Logistics, overseeing warehouse and distribution facilities across Kentucky, Tennessee, Georgia, South Carolina, and Ohio. He leads a team of site managers and holds accountability for operational performance, financial results, and customer relationships at each location.

Troy's work centers on building systems that hold up under pressure. He standardizes processes across sites, tightens inventory accuracy, and gives customers clear visibility into their operations. His background in Lean Six Sigma shapes how he approaches problems, finding the root cause rather than treating the symptom.

 

#### Chad McClung

###### Director of Information Technology

With over 15 years of professional experience, Chad brings a wealth of expertise in planning and managing desktop support, infrastructure, and networking technologies. As the leader of the Information Technology team, Chad is dedicated to driving innovation and supporting business growth through practical, efficient solutions.

Passionate about tackling complex challenges, Chad thrives on enhancing the end-user experience and fostering collaboration. His commitment to education and knowledge-sharing empowers their team and strengthens organizational success. With an Associate of Applied Business degree from Hocking College, Network+ certification, and extensive infrastructure and networking expertise, Chad is an invaluable asset to the Spartan Logistics team.

 

#### Bryonna Manes

 Bryonna Manes is a dedicated HR professional with a Bachelor of Arts in Applied Communication from Kent State University. Passionate about fostering positive employee experiences, she ensures compliance, supports development, and builds high-performing teams at Spartan Logistics. With expertise in recruitment, employee relations, and performance management, Bryonna brings a creative edge with skills in visual communication, public relations, and brand management. Currently pursuing her PHR certification, she is eager to expand her HR expertise in policy enforcement and workplace safety. 

 

#### Nate Kissel

 With 4.5 years at Spartan Logistics, including two in his current role, Nate Kissel combines expertise in operations, customer service, and efficiency. He brings 18 years of experience from "Big Box" retail management, excelling in sales, shipping, and customer service. Nate is certified as an AIB Food Defense Coordinator and PCQI and has completed the IWLA Essentials program. He leads Spartan’s food safety program, optimizes warehouse efficiency, designs product flow and safety systems, and resolves inventory challenges, all while prioritizing customer satisfaction. 

 

#### Chris Kilbarger

Chris blends operational expertise with a passion for continuous improvement. Chris excels in supply chain optimization, inventory control, and leveraging technology for efficiency. Chris’s leadership and strategic approach drive improved warehouse performance, ensuring exceptional service for clients. His blend of technical skills and team management fosters a results-driven environment, consistently meeting and exceeding operational goals.

 

#### Eric Longstreth

 With over 35 years of experience, Eric leads Spartan Logistics in driver management, transportation revenue growth, DOT compliance, and equipment management. He excels in developing creative solutions to complex challenges, using an "outside the box" approach while ensuring exceptional service. Eric is known for his collaborative style and resourcefulness, driving both organizational and personal growth. He holds a BA in Business Administration from Ohio Dominican University and is a member of the Ohio Trucking Association. His expertise includes equipment management, operational synergies, and a solution-based approach. 

 

#### Bobby Morman

###### Operations Support Manager

Bobby brings over 23 years of experience in warehouse and transportation management. With a strong logistics and supply chain operations background, he specializes in optimizing efficiency, improving processes, and driving data-based decision-making. 

Bobby is passionate about team leadership and development, fostering a positive work environment while ensuring smooth operations. His expertise extends to warehouse management systems (WMS), inventory control, troubleshooting, and strategic planning. Dedicated to building strong customer relationships and boosting morale, Bobby plays a key role in enhancing Spartan Logistics’ operational success.

 

#### Zach Sizemore

###### Asset Manager

Zach Sizemore has over 9 years of experience in material handling equipment, currently managing 160 assets across tracking, utilization, and maintenance. He focuses on delivering cost-effective, high-performance solutions to meet customer needs.

Zach is passionate about ensuring the right equipment is in place for maximum efficiency and excels in building strong vendor relationships. With 6 years of experience in maintenance for tractors, trailers, building systems, and forklifts, he brings valuable expertise to every project.

Spartan Logistics Appoints Craig Recker as VP of Operations

614-497-1777

# Spartan In The Press

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Spartan Logistics Appoints Craig Recker as Vice President of Operations

Columbus, Ohio - 4/21/2021 – Spartan Logistics is proud to announce the promotion of Craig Recker to Vice President of Operations. Craig will assume this role immediately and will oversee the daily processes of all locations.

Craig began his logistics career with Spartan in 2003 as a warehouse team member in Toledo, OH while earning a Sales and Marketing degree from the University of Toledo. Craig was promoted in 2007 to District Manager at the former Cleveland location, and later to the same position at Spartan’s Columbus locations. In 2017, Craig transitioned to the Director of Sales before returning to an operations role as a Regional Director of Operations.

In this new role, Craig will direct the strategy and execution of all 18 of Spartan’s locations which includes ensuring warehouse efficiency, operating safely, and fulfilling the customer’s needs. Spartan's President Josh Ledford says, “we are very excited to see Craig excel in this new role! His dedication to customer service and team building make him the perfect leader to take us to the next level of operational excellence company wide.”

Spartan Logistics operates industrial real estate as a third-party logistics company combined with asset-based freight services. Spartan now serves over 100 supply chain customers at 18 warehouse locations totaling over three million square feet in six states. For more information, visit spartanlogistics.com/ or call Spartan Logistics at (614) 497-1777.

2024-06-27 Women Empowering Women - CSCMP - Council of Supply Chain Management Professionals

# 2024-06-27 Women Empowering Women

## Women Empowering Women

Thursday, June 27, 2024

### CSCMP Chicago is pleased to present our Women Empowering Women event!

Women to Women panel – June 27, 2024.

Event Overview:

Embark on a journey through the supply chain industry from a unique perspective: that of women leaders. This panel of esteemed figures will openly share their experiences as minorities within the ecosystem, shedding light on both the triumphs and tribulations encountered throughout their careers.

Explore the evolving cultural landscape for inspiration on empowerment and leadership strategies designed to address industry challenges. From embracing self-acceptance to challenging stereotypes and fostering work-life balance, we’ll delve into topics crucial for professional and personal growth.

Participate in dynamic discussions centered on minority experiences and pathways to advancement, guided by seasoned industry leaders. Expect invaluable insights, networking opportunities, and mentorship guidance to propel your journey forward.

This event guarantees empowerment, meaningful connections, and individual development. Secure your spot at the CSCMP Chicago Women’s Event and join us for an enriching experience!

#### MEET OUR SPEAKERS:

Amber Romando 

Chief Operating Officer Spartan Logistics 

Amber Romando – Your host for the event

With over two decades of experience in the supply chain ecosystem, navigating her journey from a part-time transportation coordinator at UPS to currently leading the charge as the COO of Spartan Logistics, she continues to grow her network and skill sets in the supply chain world. Focusing on delivering collaboration through her simple yet powerful mantra: always ask for more. Fearlessly tackling obstacles and positioning herself at the center of every storm, she has consistently seized opportunities for growth and advancement.

She has established success with a proven track record of collaboration with small and large teams, exceeding business and personal goals and objectives and delivering profitable revenue. With a core focus on developing the culture around her teams, she believes this is the actual ingredient of any true success in the workplace.

Amber is passionate about sharing invaluable insights on leadership, teamwork, and personal growth. Her advice is not just theoretical; it’s practical and actionable, empowering you to make real changes in your career.

Charlie Saffro Chief Executive Officer CS Recruiting 

Charlie Saffro – Event Moderator 

Charlie Saffro is a recruiting expert with a passion for human leadership, talent acquisition, employee engagement, company culture and retention.

Charlie founded CS Recruiting to connect individuals to opportunities and as CEO, she manages a thriving organization and a talented team.

Charlie’s clientele includes businesses with Transportation, Logistics and Supply Chain talent needs. Her goal is to make meaningful connections that lead to long-lasting relationships.

Beyond work, she promotes personal development, mindfulness and personal growth, both in the workplace and in life.

Kim Barr Head of Business Development and Strategic Partnerships Cartesian Kinetics

Kim Barr 

A little about Kim! She is a dynamic business development leader with 17 years in the supply chain industry. Kimberly’s passion for creating innovative solutions and cultivating strong relationships is at the core of her career journey. As an Electro-Mechanical engineer, she started as a CAD drafter at an MEP firm and is now the Head of Business Development and Strategic Partnerships at Cartesian Kinetics, a rapidly growing Robotics startup company.

Kim attributes her success to hard work, respect for all(especially when it’s hard), persistence, and unapologetically being herself. These traits took years to adopt and even more years to “somewhat” master.

She strives to make an impact. Any positive impact, whether lasting a minute or for a resounding lifetime. “You never know when your words or actions will impact another human being, so always strive to do what’s right and be kind, especially when it’s hard.”

Nicole Glenn Founder and CEO Candor Expedite

Nicole Glenn 

Meet Nicole Glenn, founder and CEO of Candor Expedite, a transportation leader known for making its customers heroes by delivering creative, fast, effective, and sustainable solutions for time-sensitive and white glove shipments backed by a trusted carrier network. Today, Candor is recognized as a leading certified women-owned business headquartered in Texas – with offices in Illinois and Kansas.

Always looking for new solutions for her customers, Nicole is excited to launch “Candor Cool Chain”, a new division featuring a unique solution for shipping smaller, refrigerated and frozen packages across the U.S. — all while protecting product quality and safety, reducing wasted capacity, keeping costs under control, and minimizing environmental impact.

Nicole is a certified member of The Women’s Business Enterprise National Council, a member of The Expedite Association of North America, Women in Trucking, Women in Manufacturing, and the Transportation Intermediaries Association. She won numerous awards: Supply & Demand Chain Executive Pro’s to Know: Overall Winner; Women in Trucking’s Distinguished Women in Logistics; and Enterprising Women of the Year Champion, a tribute to the world’s top female entrepreneurs.

Kary Jablonski CEO Trucker Tools

Kary Jablonski

Kary Jablonski is Trucker Tools’ CEO and is passionate about building great teams that underpin any successful business.

Prior to Trucker Tools, she advanced through operations, logistics and strategic planning roles with Uber in the U.S. and internationally and worked as a consultant with Deloitte.

Kary currently lives in Chicago and enjoys anything active, especially running, golf and basketball.

Lindsey Martinez Director, Procurement RXO Capacity

Lindsey Martinez

“Life’s best moments usually happen unplanned” – Unknown

With a career launched by chance, Lindsey’s passion for Logistics quickly took hold, steering her toward a degree and mentors to guide her ascent up the industry ranks. Now as Director of Truckload Procurement, Lindsey pays that guidance forward, mentoring other women driven to succeed in Transportation careers.

With over a decade of Transportation leadership experience, Lindsey is an expert at exceeding business goals and driving efficiencies. As a Procurement Director, she leverages her strong Operational Management, Sales, and Customer Service skills to transform Logistics networks.

By continuously improving Procurement processes across industries, Lindsey has delivered significant cost savings and recruited top talent. Her proven track record of strengthening customer relationships through successful launches highlights her ability to be a strategic partner that creates value. With her wealth of experience across Transportation modes and Logistics, Lindsey is adept at identifying opportunities to optimize networks and exceed objectives.

With a passion for transportation and supporting underprivileged teens, Lindsey is an active member of the Detroit Transportation Club who works to provide scholarships for those in need. Driven by a desire to empower women in the industry, she serves on RXO’s ESG group “W.I.N.” (Women’s Inclusion Network) where she mentors women from diverse backgrounds, helping them grow professionally. Her dedication to uplifting others demonstrates Lindsey’s commitment to making a positive impact in the transportation sector.

Shannan Newsome Senior Vice President of Sales ABCO Systems 

Shannan Newsome

With over 23 years of experience in warehouse, transportation, logistics, supply chain, and robotic automation, Shannan is a senior sales leader who delivers results and value for her clients and company. She is currently the Senior Vice President of Sales at ABCO Systems LLC, a provider of material handling solutions engineered for today’s challenges and tomorrow’s opportunities.

Shannan has a proven track record of building and transforming sales teams, exceeding business goals and objectives, and driving revenue and profit growth. She has broad and focused functional experience in the global arena across multiple industries, modes of transportation, and systems.

Shannan is passionate about helping customers optimize their supply chain processes and leverage cutting-edge technology and automation to achieve operational excellence and competitive advantage.

### LOCATION 

 Hyatt Lodge Oak Brook 2815 Jorie Blvd Oak Brook, IL 60523 Directions

### EVENT CONTACT (thechrispride@gmail.com)

 Amber Romando: email (Amber.Romando@shipspartan.com)

All funds collected will support the CSCMP Chicago Roundtable mission of “To lead the supply chain profession by connecting, developing, and educating the world’s logistics and supply chain management professionals throughout their careers”

## Keynote: Driving Strategy through to Execution for Impact

In this keynote is to provide insights into key components needed to successfully define a strategy and see it all the way through successful execution with sustainable outcomes.

The presentation will cover elements of an effective strategy, keys to successful change management, organizational readiness, and sustainable transformation to drive long term financial impact and competitiveness.

Speaker:

- Brandi Shortt, President, ABARTA Coca-Cola Beverages

## Implementing Transformational Supply Chain Strategies Successfully

Industry research predicts that 80% of companies will embark on at least one major supply chain transformation in the next 12 to 18 months—yet fewer than 25% will achieve their intended goals. What separates success from failure?

This presentation explores the key factors behind effective supply chain transformations, with a special focus on the critical role of leadership. Gain insights from industry-leading companies and learn practical strategies to maximize your chances of success.

Speaker:

- Ignacio Arranz – Former SVP North America Supply Chain and Global Logistics at Procter & Gamble

## The Strategy-Driven Supply Chain Lab: How to cultivate strategic thinking about your supply chain

Aligning strategy, supply chain, and finance has never been more relevant. Those up to the challenge of designing the supply chain of the future not only must understand how this can be feasibly achieved based on fundamental mechanics of supply chain but also anticipate how long-term customer value creation may evolve.

While this may seem abstract, especially to pragmatic supply chain practitioners, developing such organizational muscle is no longer optional – it is an essential prerequisite for survival and success.

This presentation describes both the motivating factors and process to design a strategy-driven supply chain for the future.

- Dan Kogan – Managing Director, Strategy-Driven Supply Chain Institute

## Fixing the Foundation: How GenAI Solves Data Challenges for Supply Chain Transformation

Data continues to be the barrier to successful execution of strategic transformational initiatives. How many times have you heard “garbage in-garbage-out” when we talk about data quality?

New solutions leveraging GenAI can overcome these challenges. Global CPGs are already implementing these solutions to achieve tangible results in just few months (e.g. inventory reduction of 30%, identifying the most damaging master data issues and avoiding high costs by fixing the BOMs).

In this session you will learn from real use cases and real benefits.

- Oscar Diaz, Senior Director Supply Chain Planning, Americas Campari
- Maria Marti, CEO, Zero Error

## Adapting Supply Chain Organizational Design as Companies Grow

As small and medium-sized enterprises grow, their supply chain organizations must evolve to support increasing complexity, demand, and competition.

Designing an effective supply chain organization requires a strategic balance between flexibility, efficiency, and scalability.

This presentation explores key principles in structuring supply chain teams, defining roles, and implementing processes that align with business growth.

- Micah Bosley – Vice President of Operations and Support MSI Express

## Adapt your digital transformation to your Company’s need and culture

Digital transformation is not a one-size-fits-all journey. While new technologies promise efficiency, agility and growth, their success depends on hoe well they align with an organization’s unique needs, culture, and workforce. This conference will explore how businesses can tailor their digital transformation strategies to fit their organizational DNA, ensuring adoption scalability and long-term success. In this talk, Cristina will discuss how to:

- Customizing digital transformation to align with business goals and culture
- Overcoming resistance to change and driving adoption across teams
- The role of leadership in fostering standardization and a digital first mindset
- Key challenges and strategies to ensure a successful activation.

- Cristina Sergent – Planning Transformation & Excellence VP, Diageo

## Panel Discussion: Strengthening Supply Chains for Disaster Relief – Proactive and Reactive Strategies

In an era where disruptions—from natural disasters to global crises—are becoming more frequent and severe, the need for resilient and agile supply chains has never been greater. This panel will explore the critical role of supply chain professionals in ensuring the swift and efficient movement of essential goods, particularly in the food and beverage industry, when disaster strikes.

This discussion will bring together industry leaders to examine both proactive and reactive approaches to disaster relief planning. From preemptive strategies like predictive analytics, supplier diversification, and inventory buffering to real-time crisis response, logistics coordination, and last-mile distribution challenges, we’ll address the full spectrum of disaster preparedness and response. Attendees will gain actionable insights into mitigating risks, optimizing emergency response efforts, and leveraging technology to enhance supply chain resilience.

Join us for a dynamic discussion on how businesses can fortify their supply chains, minimize disruptions, and play a pivotal role in disaster relief efforts—ensuring that communities receive the critical resources they need when they need them most.

Moderator: Amber Romando – CEO of Spartan Logistics and CSCMP Chicago Roundtable President Elect

- Brian Boston – Director of Sales, Prosponsive Logistics
- Robert Levy – Sr Director of Transportation for Feeding America
- Cory O’Connor – Director of Customer Service and Logistics, The Jel Sert Company

## All That and a Bag of Chalk: Being the Connection

A well-structured supply chain is the backbone of innovation and product excellence. This session will explore how supply chain integration with engineering and product development ensures efficient sourcing, production, and distribution while maintaining the highest standards of safety and performance.

With a focus on durability and low-maintenance innovation, we will discuss strategies for meeting global demand efficiently. The session will also highlight key shifts in supply chain strategy from pre- to post-COVID, including how to navigate disruptions, optimize inventory, and build long-term resilience in an evolving market

- Scott Thomas, Supply Chain Director, Head Rush Technologies

## The Hero’s Journey in the Age of AI Optimization: Lessons from UPS and Beyond

Supply chain professionals are no strangers to investigating the latest AI technologies to optimize their supply chain performance. However, successful adoption isn’t automatic—it requires vision, expertise, and persistence.

Drawing from the compelling story of Jack Levis at UPS and his pioneering journey deploying the ORION AI optimization system, Steve Sashihara introduces a transformative metric called “Percent Optimal,” now possible through advanced AI.

Attendees will learn how this KPI shifts operational performance measurements from traditional benchmarks toward striving for optimal outcomes. By identifying Unique Value Activities (UVAs) and systematically applying AI-driven insights, organizations can drive meaningful and sustainable improvements within their supply chains.

- Steve Sashihara – CEO Princeton Consultants

## Changing the Narrative- How to Move Supply Chain from Cost Center to Strategic Asset in a Manufacturing Organization

For a manufacturer, supply chain costs typically account for 10-20% of total revenue and are commonly perceived as an unavoidable burden. Schreiber Foods, an $8 billion-dollar global food manufacturer has been on a journey to monetize Supply Chain as a Service. Through a newly created business unit, the Company is gaining a better understanding of the value that supply chain can bring to the bottom line in addition to becoming a more strategic supplier.

In this thought-provoking session, Nate will share how this business model is creating value for Schreiber’s customers including Retailers, Distributors, and other Food Manufacturers, while increasing EBITDA for the organization.

- Nate Shillington, Vice President of Distribution, Schreiber Foods

## Keynote Panel: Supply Chain 2030: Key Trends and How to Stay Ahead

The supply chain landscape is shifting faster than ever, shaped by geopolitical uncertainties, rapid technological advancements, evolving consumer demands, sustainability imperatives, and a changing workforce. Organizations must not only adapt to these forces but also proactively build strategies that drive resilience, efficiency, and competitive advantage.

In this dynamic panel discussion, industry leaders will explore the most pressing trends impacting supply chains today and how companies are addressing them. Panelists will discuss the structural and organizational shifts required to thrive in this evolving environment, key challenges businesses will face, and actionable strategies to future-proof operations.

Attendees will gain insights into how top companies are integrating new technologies, redefining workforce needs, strengthening supplier networks, and balancing efficiency with sustainability. Join us to uncover what it takes to build a supply chain that is not just reactive—but built for long-term success in an unpredictable world.
